entries.title: Proverbs 7:1
segments:
CHAP. VII. 
 
  An exhortation to cleave to wisdom, as a preservative from strange   women, ver. 1-5.   The snares they lay for unwary young men, ver. 6-23.   A serious caution against coming near them, ver. 24-27.

entries.title: Proverbs 7:2
segments: V. 2. Live-Thou shalt live.  Eye-With all possible care and diligence.

entries.title: Proverbs 7:3
segments: V. 3. Bind them-As a ring which is continually in a man's eye.

entries.title: Proverbs 7:4
segments: V. 4. And call-Acquaint and delight thyself with her.

entries.title: Proverbs 7:8
segments: V. 8. Passing-Idle and careless, near the corner of the street in which her house stood.

entries.title: Proverbs 7:12
segments: V. 12. Without-Without the door of her house.  Corner-Of the streets, where she might either conceal or discover herself, as she saw fit.

entries.title: Proverbs 7:14
segments: V. 14. Offerings-I have paid my peace-offerings which I had vowed. Whereby she signifies, that she had plentiful provisions at her house for his entertainment. For the peace-offerings were to be of the best flesh,
, and a considerable part of these offerings fell to the offerer's share.

entries.title: Proverbs 7:20
segments: V. 20. Hath taken-Which is an evidence that he designs to stay a considerable time.  At the day-So that we need not fear any surprise.

entries.title: Proverbs 7:22
segments: V. 22. As an ox-Going to it securely, as if it were going to a good pasture.

entries.title: Proverbs 7:23
segments: V. 23. His liver-His vital parts, 'till his life be lost.
